title: Who registers with whom: the agent and the connector, not PingOne
lede: PingOne has no dynamic client registration and no CIMD, so the connector ends the registration itself. The agent's client ID never reaches PingOne.

lanes.label: Registration is between the agent and the connector; the connector signs in at PingOne with its own client ID

nodes.label: 2. Connector hands out a client ID
sub: a muse- ID, kept only in the connector's memory

nodes.label: 3. Agent starts a sign-in
sub: its muse- ID, its own redirect address, PKCE S256

nodes.label: 4. Connector checks it
sub: the redirect must match the registration exactly

nodes.label: 5. Connector signs in with its OWN app
sub: its own PingOne client ID and callback; login hint marked .conn

nodes.label: 6. PingOne signs the user in
sub: it knows the connector's app, never the agent

nodes.label: Never sent to PingOne
sub: the agent's muse- ID, redirect address and registration

nodes.label: 7. Connector swaps the PingOne code
sub: acts for the user; keeps the PingOne tokens

nodes.label: 8. Agent gets the connector's own token
sub: opaque, issued by the connector, not by PingOne

steps.title: Registers
steps.what: The agent registers at the connector's /connector/register with its redirect address. This is dynamic client registration (RFC 7591).
steps.why: PingOne cannot do this, so the connector does it for the agent.

steps.title: Client ID
steps.what: The connector answers with a client ID that starts muse-. It lives only in the connector's memory.
steps.why: It is the agent's identity for the connector alone, and it is lost when the connector restarts.

steps.title: Starts sign-in
steps.what: The agent opens /connector/authorize with that ID, its redirect address and a PKCE challenge.
steps.why: This is the normal OAuth code flow with PKCE, aimed at the connector.

steps.title: Checked
steps.what: The connector refuses an unknown ID or a redirect that does not match the registration exactly.
steps.why: A bad request never gets redirected anywhere.

steps.title: Own client ID
steps.what: The connector sends the user to PingOne with its own PingOne client ID, its own callback and a login hint marked .conn.
steps.why: PingOne sees a known app, so no registration at PingOne is needed.

steps.title: Not sent
steps.what: The agent's muse- ID, its redirect address and its registration are not sent to PingOne.
steps.why: If the agent used its muse- ID at PingOne directly, PingOne would refuse it as unknown.

steps.title: Code back
steps.what: PingOne signs the user in and returns a code to the connector's callback. The connector swaps it and acts for the user.
steps.why: The PingOne tokens stay with the connector.

steps.title: Own token
steps.what: The connector gives the agent its own one-time code, and the agent trades it, with its PKCE verifier, for the connector's own token.
steps.why: The agent holds a connector token, never a PingOne token.
